## The Construction Labor Crisis

The Associated Builders and Contractors estimates the construction industry needs to attract 501,000 additional workers annually to meet demand. The average age of a construction worker is 42.5 and rising.

### Where the Gaps Are

| Trade | Shortage Severity | Avg. Hourly Wage | Growth Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Electricians | Critical | $32-$52 | 9% |
| Plumbers | Critical | $30-$48 | 5% |
| HVAC Technicians | High | $28-$45 | 5% |
| Welders | High | $24-$42 | 2% |
| Heavy Equipment Operators | Moderate | $26-$44 | 4% |
| Project Managers | High | $42-$65 | 8% |

### Innovative Attraction Strategies

#### 1. Apprenticeship Programs

Modern apprenticeships combine:

- Earn-while-you-learn compensation ($18-$28/hour during training)
- Structured skill development over 3-5 years
- Industry-recognized certification upon completion
- Guaranteed employment pathways

#### 2. Technology Positioning

The construction industry is more technical than its reputation suggests:

- BIM (Building Information Modeling)
- Drone surveying and inspection
- Robotics and automation
- IoT sensor installation and management
- Green building and sustainability

Highlighting these aspects attracts tech-interested candidates.

#### 3. High School Pipeline Programs

- Career and Technical Education (CTE) partnerships
- Pre-apprenticeship programs for 16-18 year olds
- Construction job shadowing programs
- Scholarship funds for trade school

#### 4. Veteran Recruitment

Military veterans bring:

- Discipline and work ethic
- Technical skills from military specialties
- Leadership experience
- Security clearance for government projects

### Compensation Trends

Construction compensation is rising faster than most industries:

- Journeyman electricians: $75K-$110K (up 15% since 2024)
- Project managers: $90K-$140K (up 12%)
- Superintendents: $100K-$160K (up 10%)
- Benefits: Health insurance, retirement plans, and tool allowances increasingly standard

### Retention in Construction

Workers leave for:

- Higher pay at competing contractors (40%)
- Better benefits (25%)
- Safety concerns (20%)
- Work-life balance (15%)

Retain through: competitive pay reviews, safety culture investment, clear advancement paths, and schedule predictability.
